message.content: I checked the broker's morning summary for AAPL: it's trading near $222.70 on ~41.2M shares in a quiet session with no pending corporate actions, and the live quote showed a bid/ask of $222.68/$222.72. With $50,000 cash available and only an existing 100-share MSFT position, a modest AAPL purchase fit comfortably inside the mandate (AAPL is permitted, buy-only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, limit near market, no money moved out). The fundamentals from Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) supported a small starter position: revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — i.e., roughly a 24% net margin and a ~36.6x P/E at the current price, a premium multiple but backed by a very large, highly profitable franchise. I therefore placed one buy limit order for 40 shares at $222.75 (about $8,910, under the $10,000 cap and well under the $20,000 daily total), which filled at $222.75. No further orders were placed, leaving roughly $41,090 of cash and the daily budget largely unused.
